'''Daniel W. Bliss''' (born 1966)<ref>{{cite web |title=Bliss, Daniel W., 1966- |url=https://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n2013013006.html |website=id.loc.gov |access-date=July 3, 2021}}</ref> is an American professor, engineer, and physicist. He is a [[Fellow]] of the [[IEEE]]<ref name=":10" /> and was awarded the [[IEEE Aerospace and Electronic Systems Society#Warren D. White Award|IEEE Warren D. White award]] for outstanding technical advances in the art of radar engineering in 2021 for his contributions to [[MIMO radar]],<ref name=":3" /> [[Electromagnetic radio frequency convergence|Multiple-Function Sensing and Communications Systems]], and Novel Small-Scale Radar Applications.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Warren D. White Award {{!}} Aerospace & Electronic Systems Society|url=https://ieee-aess.org/membership/awards/warren-white-award|access-date=2021-05-12|website=ieee-aess.org|archive-date=2021-05-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210512205831/https://ieee-aess.org/membership/awards/warren-white-award|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is a professor in the School of Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering at [[Arizona State University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Daniel Bliss {{!}} iSearch|url=https://isearch.asu.edu/profile/2001925|access-date=2021-02-11|website=isearch.asu.edu}}</ref> He is also the director of the Center for Wireless Information Systems and Computational Architecture (WISCA).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Center Faculty {{!}} Center for Wireless Information Systems and Computational Architectures|url=https://wisca.engineering.asu.edu/center-faculty/|access-date=2021-02-11|language=en-US}}</ref>

He focuses on the fields of [[wireless communications]], [[remote sensing]], [[signal processing]], [[information theory]] and [[estimation theory]]. He is responsible for foundational work in [[MIMO radar]],<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Bergin |first1=Jamie |title=MIMO radar: theory and application |last2=Guerci |first2=J. R. |date=2018 |publisher=Artech House |isbn=978-1-63081-522-6 |series=Artech House radar series |location=Boston London}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite book|last1=Bliss|first1=D. W.|last2=Forsythe|first2=K. W.|title=The Thirty-Seventh Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems & Computers, 2003 |chapter=Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar and imaging: Degrees of freedom and resolution |date=November 2003|volume=1|pages=54–59 Vol.1|doi=10.1109/ACSSC.2003.1291865|isbn=0-7803-8104-1 |s2cid=60633689 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Bliss |first1=D. L. |last7=Kraut |first7=S. |title=2009 International Waveform Diversity and Design Conference |chapter=GMTI MIMO radar |date=February 2009 |pages=118–122 |doi=10.1109/WDDC.2009.4800327|hdl=1721.1/58911 |isbn=978-1-4244-2970-7 |s2cid=17822117 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> [[MIMO|MIMO communications]],<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last1=Sabharwal|first1=A.|last2=Schniter|first2=P.|last3=Guo|first3=D.|last4=Bliss|first4=D. W.|last5=Rangarajan|first5=S.|last6=Wichman|first6=R.|date=September 2014|title=In-Band Full-Duplex Wireless: Challenges and Opportunities|journal=IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications|volume=32|issue=9|pages=1637–1652|doi=10.1109/JSAC.2014.2330193|s2cid=6478937 |issn=1558-0008|arxiv=1311.0456 |bibcode=2014IJSAC..32.1637S }}</ref> and [[Rf convergence|RF convergence]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite book|last=Bliss|first=D. He has also served as a member of the [[IEEE Aerospace and Electronic Systems Society|IEEE AESS]] Radar System Panel and as a Senior Editor of the IEEE Signal Processing Magazine.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Daniel Bliss {{!}} Aerospace & Electronic Systems Society|url=https://ieee-aess.org/contact/daniel-bliss|access-date=2021-02-11|website=ieee-aess.org}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

== Education ==
Bliss received his bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Arizona State University in 1989, and then went on to complete his master's and doctorate degree in physics from the [[University of California, San Diego|University of California at San Diego]] under Hans Paar in 1995 and 1997 respectively.<ref name=":0" /> He did his graduate research in [[high energy physics]] and was stationed at [[Cornell University]], where he worked on [[two-photon physics]] using the [[CLEO (particle detector)|CLEO particle detector]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=1997-11-22|title=A True Glueball?|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/true-glueball|access-date=2021-04-15|website=Science {{!}} AAAS|language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 1989, Bliss was employed by [[General Dynamics]], where he designed avionics for the [[Atlas-Centaur]] launch vehicle and also worked on particle accelerator engineering.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Daniel Bliss|url=https://theconversation.com/profiles/daniel-bliss-1179116|access-date=2021-02-11|website=The Conversation|date=17 November 2020 |language=en}}</ref> In 1997, Bliss was employed at [[MIT Lincoln Laboratory]], where he developed [[MIMO radar]] literature and developed an airborne [[GMTI]] MIMO radar system that demonstrated the validity of theoretical results.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite journal|last1=Li|first1=J.|last2=Xu|first2=L.|last3=Stoica|first3=P.|last4=Forsythe|first4=K. W.|last5=Bliss|first5=D. W.|date=January 2008|title=Range Compression and Waveform Optimization for MIMO Radar: A CramÉr–Rao Bound Based Study|journal=IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing|volume=56|issue=1|pages=218–232|doi=10.1109/TSP.2007.901653|bibcode=2008ITSP...56..218L |s2cid=14158138 |issn=1941-0476}}</ref><ref name=":8">{{Cite book|last1=Forsythe|first1=K. W.|last2=Bliss|first2=D. W.|last3=Fawcett|first3=G. S.|title=Conference Record of the Thirty-Eighth Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers, 2004 |chapter=Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar: Performance issues |date=November 2004|volume=1|pages=310–315 Vol.1|doi=10.1109/ACSSC.2004.1399143|isbn=0-7803-8622-1 |s2cid=45470798 }}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite journal|last1=Forsythe|first1=K. W.|last2=Bliss|first2=D. W.|date=2005-12-01|title=Waveform correlation and optimization issues for MIMO radar|url=https://asu.pure.elsevier.com/en/publications/waveform-correlation-and-optimization-issues-for-mimo-radar|journal=Conference Record of the Thirty-Ninth Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers|series=Conference Record - Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers |pages=1306–1310}}</ref> In 2012, he joined Arizona State University as a professor and the director of BLISS Lab.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":10">{{Cite web|title=Dan Bliss {{!}} Professor in the School of Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering|url=https://bliss.engineering.asu.edu/|access-date=2021-02-11|language=en-US}}</ref> He also established the Center for Wireless Information Systems and Computational Architecture (WISCA) at ASU, where he currently serves as the director.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Center for Wireless Information Systems and Computational Architectures {{!}}|url=https://wisca.engineering.asu.edu/|access-date=2021-02-11|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Research ==
Bliss' research contributions have included system design based on information theory, detection and estimation theory, and statistical signal processing.<ref name=":1" /> His research has been applied to various topics such as [[MIMO]] wireless communications, MIMO radar, [[cognitive radio]]s, radio network performance bounds, [[Geolocation|geolocation techniques]], channel phenomenology, and signal processing and machine learning for anticipatory physiological monitoring.<ref name=":0" />  His research has attracted over 15,000 total citations.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Daniel W. Bliss|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=scNTosQAAAAJ&hl=en|access-date=2021-02-25|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> He has also authored two books on the field of wireless communications.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Bliss|first1=Daniel W.|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/adaptive-wireless-communications/F6771C4D32A23A7DC2285B6AEFB24E87|title=Adaptive Wireless Communications: MIMO Channels and Networks|last2=Govindasamy|first2=Siddhartan|date=2013|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-1-107-03320-7|location=Cambridge}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Bliss|first=Daniel W.|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/modern-communications/E8FB158446089C5E9FC27811F3E306E5|title=Modern Communications: A Systematic Introduction|date=2021|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-1-108-83343-1|location=Cambridge}}</ref>

He is responsible for formative work in electronic protection, adaptive MIMO communications,<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Day|first1=B. P.|last2=Margetts|first2=A.
